claims: A canonical protocol-machine program now owns the measured record, event, instruction, transition, effect, and refusal vocabulary.
A separately identified policy program owns exact required checks, outcome controls, and precedence; missing checks refuse rather than becoming implicit UNKNOWN results.
The normative profile binds machine and policy identities, and the private partial effective contract binds that profile to the exact validated fact-set hash.

The generic Python interpreter validates complete operand and identity closure, stages effects atomically, refuses hostile artifacts and prestates deliberately, and replays deterministically without fixture vocabulary, callbacks, I/O, or graph access.
All 66 focused M1 and M2 tests passed and final independent review found no P0 through P2 issue in the declared private boundary.
limitations: CC-R11 remains ACTIVE because the public KnowledgeChangeSet, empty-genesis history, replay-derived Small Shop graph, and runner are not implemented.
This is not the full three-role EffectiveContract composition, public API, Assent cutover, or cross-language parity proof.
The full repository pytest run was deliberately interrupted after 806 passes and no failures because its runtime exceeded the Pareto gate; package and release checks were excluded.

why: The evidence establishes that machine and policy meaning are explicit, identified data and that Python is only the generic interpreter for this measured slice, while preserving the remaining public change-set, history, projection, and portability work as explicit debt.
